subject: PrimeCare launch - temporary rate policy override request
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@primecare.health>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary spike capacity for launch next week
Attachments: primecare-traffic-plan.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from PrimeCare — we go live with a pilot on May 31 and expect a sharp spike in inference traffic for the first 48-72 hours as we onboard initial clinics. Our platform will route real-time triage prompts to Redwood and we estimate peak sustained QPS of ~300-400 for short windows, with normal baseline ~30 QPS.

Current contracted burst quota at our tier is 100 QPS and we will hit throttling quickly. Can Redwood temporarily raise our burst limit (or create a short-lived allowance) for the launch window? We can accept conditional caps, limited time windows, and cost add-ons. Attached is the traffic plan and expected hourly profile.

Please advise required steps (security paperwork, cost, any gating). Also looping Eli (ops) who will own traffic throttling on our side.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Director, Product
PrimeCare Health

---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary spike capacity for launch next week

Forwarding — PrimeCare requests a temporary rate/burst override for an imminent pilot. They attached a traffic plan; baseline is low but they expect short spikes to 300-400 QPS.

Internal ask: can we provision a time-boxed override (config + billing flag) and what security/contract items do we need? Vivek/Karthik can you weigh in on pricing and approval flow; Aditya, quick security check on logs/audit & any required addenda. Lauren — want to keep you in the loop given this is a launch that could escalate to an enterprise commit.

Key constraints they said they will accept: limited window, capped peak, signed amendment/DocuSign, and monitoring/alerts.

I propose we avoid changing their permanent quota; prefer a temporary policy override tied to deal RDW-9872.

— Soojin
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary spike capacity for launch next week

Thanks — I reviewed the traffic plan. Suggest we approve a short-lived override with conditions:
- Window: 2027-06-03 00:00 UTC to 2027-06-10 23:59 UTC (customer requested initial 7 days; propose symmetrical window)
- Cap: hard peak cap at 350 QPS (soft threshold alerts at 250 QPS)
- Ramp: 24-hour ramp to peak where we gradually increase batch size/routing to avoid KV cache pressure
- Pricing: 15% surcharge on metered usage during the override window (applies to token charges only)
- Billing/contract: require a signed amendment/DocuSign before enabling

Engineering inputs: please confirm which model variant (gpt-3.5-ish or quantized redwood-light) we route for this window; prefer a quantized variant to limit memory pressure. Karthik, can you generate an amendment template and a short invoice?

If security sign-off is clean, I’m okay to approve on sales side.

— Vivek
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary spike capacity for launch next week — security checklist

On Tue, May 31, 2027 at 10:22 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — I reviewed the traffic plan. Suggest we approve a short-lived override with conditions:
> - Window: 2027-06-03 00:00 UTC to 2027-06-10 23:59 UTC
> - Cap: hard peak cap at 350 QPS ...
>

Quick security notes:
- Reviewed PrimeCare's info and the attached traffic plan; no immediate data-residency red flags.
- Require signed BAA addendum and DocuSign amendment before we flip the flag.
- Must enable enhanced audit logging for the override period (retain 90 days beyond window) and route logs to our secure bucket with customer-facing access controls documented.
- Recommend we isolate their workload onto a dedicated serving pool (if capacity allows) or tag requests for filtering; this prevents unfair cache pollution across tenants.
- KMS: if PrimeCare requests customer-managed keys we need the KMS details; otherwise we use platform KMS with audit hooks.

Attachments: SOC2-type2-summary.pdf — their security questionnaire looks reasonable but amendment required.

Operational timeline: security sign-off + DocuSign executed => 24 hours to enable the override (we need ops runbook + preflight tests).

— Aditya Rao
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@primecare.health>, Eli Turner <eli.turner@primecare.health>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Approved: temporary override granted (conditions & next steps)

Hi Maya / Eli — following internal review, Redwood can grant a time-boxed policy override for PrimeCare's launch with the following binding conditions: 

1) Window: 2027-06-03 00:00 UTC through 2027-06-10 23:59 UTC (7 full days).
2) Technical cap: hard peak at 350 QPS. We will configure soft alerts at 250 QPS and initiate throttling at the hard cap.
3) Ramp: 24-hour controlled ramp to peak; please coordinate with Eli to stage traffic.
4) Pricing: 15% surcharge on token usage during the window; an invoice and DocuSign amendment (RDW-9872 amendment) must be signed prior to enablement.
5) Security: Signed BAA addendum + DocuSign amendment required. Redwood will enable enhanced audit logging (90-day retention) and tag requests for isolation as discussed.
6) Operational: Once DocuSign & signed amendment are received and preflight tests pass, ops needs up to 24 hours to flip the override. We will monitor dashboards closely and provide a single point-of-contact (Vivek) during the window.

Attachments included for your reference: primecare-traffic-plan.pdf, primecare-sla-proposal.xlsx, SOC2-type2-summary.pdf. DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/1234-SIGN-4521. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567.

Next steps for PrimeCare: please review and sign the amendment, confirm KMS preference if any, and reply with a final traffic cut schedule (start times in UTC). We will not enable the override until DocuSign is executed.

Happy to jump on a 15-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Soogjin Lee
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183
